provenance_note: The isolated gateway served the personal-shopper app built into the Kiro Crew checkout (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/personal_shopper, website/src/apps/personal-shopper). This repository is the externally packaged copy of that app; PORTING.md lists where the two differ.

setup.name: retire the host's one-time startup intro

body.text: Running shoes: US 9.5, wide toe box
Jackets: size M, but sleeves run short on most brands
Happy to pay more for a 5-year warranty
Small kitchen: nothing wider than 30 cm on the counter
Niece Mira (9) loves astronomy and drawing

body.problem: Birthday gift for my niece, who loves astronomy
body.advice: At nine, a hands-on gift she can use without an adult beats a fragile telescope. Pair something for clear nights with something for cloudy ones.

body.problem: Our living room echoes on video calls
body.advice: Hard floors and bare walls bounce sound. A large rug and the bookshelf moved to the empty wall absorb most of it; acoustic panels are not needed for a room this size.

body.problem: My knees ache after weekend 10K runs
body.advice: Your current pair is a minimal-cushion trainer. Try the gravel path for two weeks first; if the ache stays, a high-cushion daily trainer in a wide fit is worth it.

data_notes: History entries carry the date they were saved: the app stamps each entry with the gateway's own clock and its API takes no date, so every entry shows the capture day.
History was filled through POST /api/apps/personal-shopper/history. Nothing in the app's UI or the advisor writes History today, so the README shows that picture as example data.

The chat scenes ran on a live model (see agent_backend). The gateway's approval mode is 'reads', which approves web page fetches but declined the advisor's web searches, and the stores are fictional .example sites that cannot be opened, so the advisor read no store page: the prices in its replies are its own rough guesses, as it says.
